newsitem.title: USA: Met Life offers stock fund for retirement plans.
newsitem.headline: Met Life offers stock fund for retirement plans.

text.p: Metropolitan Life Insurance Co said it unveiled a mutual fund aimed at reducing the dangers for companies with pension plans that are over-concentrated in their own corporate stock.
The MetLife Diversified Employer Stock Fund is a pooled equity fund that would consist of the stocks of participating companies.

MetLife said the fund was created as a way to hedge against unexpected and uncontrolled volatility and risk when a pension plan concentrates most or all of its pension investments in its own corporate stock.
Employer pension plans that are invested solely in the company's own stock run the risk of losing value if the stock price declines.
Under the plan, contributions made with a company's common stock will purchase units of the fund.

Jeff Norris, vice president for pension product marketing, said MetLife has just begun to market the fund, and has not yet signed on any corporate clients. In a test market with eight corporations, MetLife found at least three "were seriously interested."
MetLife has 300 corporater clients that receive some type of pension product or service, including 60 of the Fortune 100 companies.
